newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African ministers to fast forward economic plans.
newsitem.headline: S.African ministers to fast forward economic plans.

text.p: South Africa has set up a programme for implementation this year of its macro-economic strategy for growth, employment and redistribution, known as GEAR, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Friday.

Expanding on President Nelson Mandela's opening address to parliament, Mboweni, who heads the policy unit of the ruling African National Congress (ANC), said individual ministers would announce specific plans during budget debates over the next few months.
He said Mandela was signalling an intention to accelerate delivery to the country's poorest.
"The President was blowing the whistle for a starting up line that will ensure that we move a little bit faster. That whistle has been blown," Mboweni said at a news conference.
"We don't want to take the sting away from the announcements that the ministers will be making over the next couple of days and in particular during their budget votes, which are policy statements.

"But what has definitely happened is that we have, through the guidance of the deputy president (Thabo Mbeki) in particular, gone through an intensive programme during the course of the last year which has resulted in us having a clear programme of action on how to implement GEAR," he said.
Justice Minister Dullah Omar said the government was also working on legislation to eliminate corruption from the judicial process - courts and police - as a first step towards reducing crime levels.
He said courts would be given better information and bail conditions would be made tougher for some crimes than for others to ensure that dangerous criminals are not released too easily.
Omar said Mandela's speech had been a realistic catalogue of achievements and plans, adding: "There are no false promises, but it is an optimistic speech."
